explain.say: Imagine a village square in Guinea at sunset. One drum speaks, the others answer, and everyone starts to dance. That drum is the djembe, from the Mandé peoples of West Africa, in countries like Mali and Guinea. It makes three main sounds. Look at the board.

explain.say: Look at the bass. Hit the centre of the skin with your flat palm and let your hand bounce off. Boom! It is the lowest, deepest sound. Try patting your knee in the middle with a flat hand. Can you make it bounce?

explain.say: Now the tone. Keep your fingers together and strike near the edge, so the fingers hit the skin and the palm stays on the rim. It makes a round, clear note, higher than the bass. Where on the drum is the tone played?

groups.ask: What is a slap on the djembe?

explain.say: Look at the slap. Strike near the edge again, but with relaxed fingers that snap away, like flicking water. Crack! It is the highest, sharpest sound. Bass, tone, slap: low, middle, high. Can you say them in order?

explain.say: Brilliant drumming! The music works by call and response: look at the circle. The leader calls, the group answers, the big dunun drums keep time and the dancers move. Wow fact: each djembe is carved from one single log and topped with goatskin, tightened with rope. Challenge: play bass, tone, tone, slap on a table!

faq.q: How do you play a bass on the djembe?
faq.a: Strike the centre of the drumhead with a flat, relaxed palm and let it bounce off. It makes the deepest sound of the djembe.
asks: How do I make a low sound on the djembe?

faq.a: A tone is played near the edge with the fingers held together, flat on the skin, while the palm rests on the rim. It gives a round, clear, middle sound.
asks: How do I play a djembe tone?

faq.q: What is a slap on the djembe?
faq.a: A slap is played near the edge like a tone, but with loose fingers that whip onto the skin and snap away. It is the highest, sharpest djembe sound.

Why is my slap not loud?

faq.q: Where does the djembe come from?
faq.a: The djembe comes from the Mandé peoples of West Africa, in today's Mali, Guinea and nearby countries. It is now played all over the world.
Call and response is when a leader plays or sings a phrase and the group answers. It is central to West African drumming and singing, and is heard in gospel, blues and many other styles.

facts: The djembe originated among the Mandé peoples of West Africa, in the region of present-day Mali and Guinea.
A traditional djembe is carved from a single piece of hardwood, with a goatskin head tuned by rope.

quiz.say: Which djembe stroke makes the lowest sound?
quiz.show: The lowest djembe sound is the…
quiz.why: The bass, played with a flat palm in the centre, is the deepest sound.

wrong.1: The tone is a middle, round sound played near the edge.
wrong.2: The slap is the highest, sharpest sound.

quiz.say: The lead drummer plays a phrase and everyone answers. What is this called?
quiz.show: Leader plays, group answers. This is…
quiz.why: A leader calls and the group responds.

wrong.1: A solo is one person playing alone.
wrong.2: Tuning is tightening the drum, not a musical pattern.
